newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury sees moderate growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury sees moderate growth, low inflation.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury expects the economy to grow at around two percent in the second half of this year, roughly the same pace of growth seen in the second quarter, while inflation should remain subdued, a Treasury official said on Tuesday.

"The economy appears to have returned close to trend in the second quarter," Treasury's John Auten said in a statement. "Looking forward to the second half of the year, it seems probable that the economy will move closer to trend -- closer to two percent growth."
"With increased inflationary pressures notable by their absence, the outlook for the economy is very promising," Auten added.

He said most statistical evidence pointed to a growth rate of around two percent in the second quarter of this year. With the six percent growth recorded in the first quarter, that would average at four percent for the first half.
First official gross domestic product estimates for the second quarter are due to be released on Thursday.
Auten added that the Treasury expected good inflation performance to continue along a path of moderate growth.
"With commodity prices flat or falling, demand inflation is virtually non-existent," he said. "Overheating seems almost an archaic term." ((- Washington newsroom 202-898 8377))
